title: Preferential CO oxidation (PROX) reference family
objective: Optional literature-backed reference family for sanity-checking catalyst economics for preferential CO oxidation, the reformate clean-up step that protects PEM fuel-cell anodes. COMET itself remains reaction-agnostic and this family is a screening aid, not a process design.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Balance economics, source confidence, route confidence, and performance.

cost-first.label: Cost-first
cost-first.description: Bias ranking toward selling cost while keeping route and evidence guardrails.

evidence-first.label: Evidence-first
evidence-first.description: Reward transparent, higher-confidence pricing and more reproducible routes.

citations.label: ACS Catal. 2012
citations.note: Review of preferential CO oxidation over platinum-group-metal catalysts.

citations.label: Catal. Today 2009
citations.note: Park's review of selective CO removal from hydrogen-rich streams.

citations.label: J. Catal. 1997
citations.note: Benchmark Pt/Al2O3 PROX kinetics: ~80% CO conversion near 200 C, Ea 71 kJ/mol, orders -0.4 in CO and +0.8 in O2.

citations.label: Catal. Today 2000
citations.note: Fe-oxide-promoted Pt monolith for fuel-cell PROX: 68% CO conversion at 90 C vs 13% unpromoted.

citations.label: Appl. Catal. A 2002
citations.note: Structural study of the Fe-oxide-promoted Pt/alumina PROX catalyst.

citations.label: J. Catal. 1993
citations.note: Oh and Sinkevitch's original selective-CO-oxidation screening for fuel-cell feeds.

citations.label: J. Catal. 1993
citations.note: Haruta's foundational size/support rules for low-temperature CO oxidation on sub-4-nm gold.

citations.label: Catal. Lett. 2001
citations.note: PROX-specific screening of Au on seven supports at 80 C: reducible-oxide supports up to 10x more active; carbonate deactivation identified.

citations.label: J. Catal. 1999
citations.note: Au/alpha-Fe2O3 PROX kinetics at 40-100 C: ~75% selectivity at 80 C, Ea 31 kJ/mol.

citations.label: Chem. Lett. 1987
citations.note: The original far-below-0-C gold CO-oxidation communication.

citations.label: Catal. Lett. 2001
citations.note: Coprecipitated CuO-CeO2 PROX: very active, exceptionally selective, resistant to CO2 and H2O.

citations.label: Catal. Today 2002
citations.note: Head-to-head Pt vs Au vs CuO-CeO2 comparison under realistic reformate feeds.

citations.label: Appl. Catal. A 2003
citations.note: Urea-nitrate combustion synthesis of CuO-CeO2 with copper-content optimization.

route_templates.name: Pt-Fe impregnation with monolith washcoating
route_templates.manufacturing_mode: Washcoated cordierite honeycomb for fuel processors
preprocess: Pt and Fe salt solution make-up
synthesis: Impregnation of the alumina with Pt then Fe promoter
route_templates.route_note: Deployed washcoated on ceramic honeycombs in commercial fuel processors per the cited monolith study. Small-scale step availability: continuous units swapped for their batch/small siblings.

route_templates.name: Chloride-free gold deposition-precipitation
route_templates.manufacturing_mode: Powder or washcoat, strict size control
preprocess: Support slurry preparation (TiO2, CeO2 or Fe2O3)
HAuCl4 solution make-up with pH control
synthesis: Deposition-precipitation of gold at controlled pH
postprocess: Air calcination fixing sub-4-nm hemispherical Au
route_templates.route_note: Chloride-free deposition-precipitation and sub-4-nm size control are the documented make-or-break constraints for nanogold. Small-scale step availability: continuous units swapped for their batch/small siblings.

route_templates.name: Urea-nitrate combustion of CuO-CeO2
preprocess: Copper and cerium nitrate solution make-up
Urea dosing to the target fuel ratio
synthesis: Urea-nitrate combustion to nanocrystalline mixed oxide
route_templates.route_note: Combustion synthesis is documented as simple and fast to a nanocrystalline product; the direct-fired kiln proxies the combustion/ignition stage. Small-scale step availability: continuous units swapped for their batch/small siblings.

candidates.title: Fe-promoted Pt/Al2O3 (fuel-processor standard)
candidates.summary: 0.5 wt% Pt on alumina with an iron-oxide promoter, washcoated on honeycombs: the deployed fuel-processor PROX catalyst, with Fe promotion pulling operation from ~200 C down to 90 C.
decision_notes: The de-risked choice with the deepest kinetics record; platinum inventory is the cost driver at sub-percent loadings.
Fe promoter screened at 0.5 wt%: the promotion effect is source-quoted, its exact loading is not.

pricing.note: Live Pt feed with a precursor conversion markup; 0.5 wt% loading is source-quoted for the benchmark kinetics catalyst.

Contained-Fe cost from bulk synthetic black iron oxide (ICIS 2006, $0.94/lb, CatCost library), ChemPPI-escalated. The scrap-iron market feed understates precursor chemistry ~40x, so Fe components price on a precursor basis.
2025 USGS alumina import value used as a bulk oxide support proxy.

candidates.title: Au/TiO2 nanogold (low-temperature)
candidates.summary: Sub-4-nm gold on titania from chloride-free deposition-precipitation runs PROX below 100 C - the Haruta-lineage low-temperature option, bought with strict size control and carbonate-deactivation management.
decision_notes: Wins when the reformate train needs sub-100-C operation; loses on manufacturing tolerance (size control) and long-term carbonate deactivation.
Au loading screened at 2 wt%: class-typical (1-5 wt%), not stated in the fetched abstracts.

pricing.note: Live Au feed with a markup for the chloroauric-acid route; loading is a class-typical screening assumption.
2025e landed duty-paid unit value of U.S. TiO2 pigment imports, $3,200/t (USGS MCS Feb 2026).

candidates.title: CuO-CeO2 (base-metal option)
candidates.summary: Coprecipitated or combustion-made copper-ceria: very active and exceptionally selective PROX without any noble metal, tolerant of CO2 and water in realistic reformate.
decision_notes: The cost play: both oxides carry public prices and the combustion route is fast; accepts a narrower optimal window than nanogold below 100 C.
CuO screened at 7 wt%: the optimization exists in the cited full texts, the exact optimum was not abstract-verified.

pricing.note: Contained-copper basis of a ~7 wt% CuO loading with a mild precursor markup.
2025 USGS cerium-oxide price used as a bulk support proxy.
